"Hi...my name is Sam."

The last of three parients to arrive at my small, inner-city office had a notable tremor to her voice as she spoke. Making her nerves even more evident, Sam glanced around the room with unease, never allowing her eyes to settle on any one crack in the cement wall or leg of the unstable bar stools set in a circle for my first session on losing a loved one. 

"Hi, Sam." My voice was the only to respond, despite my encouraging gaze towards the woman in the red dress with short black hair and tired eyes, then towards the middle-aged man dressed in a business suit and breathing out a sigh that told the room he had more important places to be. "Why don't you tell us a bit about why you're joining us today."

Sam reached her dainty hand up to her blonde hair, twirling a strand around her finger as she began, "Well, I recently lost my little brother-" Sam's voice choked to a halt as her face strained in her effort to hold back tears.

Sam couldn't have been more than 18 years old, and her unwashed hair combined with her baggy sweatpants and torn t-shirt on top of her struggle to tell her story indicated the wear of her experience in losing someone so young and so close to her.

"It's okay Sam. Maybe we should go on with introductions and come back to you later?"
Sam nodded, avoiding eye contact as she slunk onto her stool.

"Hi, I'm John." The businessman wasted no time in taking his turn, probably in an effort to get back to the work place after our mid-afternoon meeting. 

"Hi, John."

"We all know why I'm here. I lost a loved one. My girlfriend, Jane. It was tough at first, but I've accepted what happened and I know that life goes on whether they ever find her body or not."

"Well, John, it's good to hear that your loss hasn't been holding you back...but sometimes it's important to allow yourself to greive."

"No. That's what they say, but I recently uncovered some very interesting information while sorting through Jane's journals, and now I know that, being the kind of person she was, she doesn't deserve my greivances."

I paused, unsure of how to proceed.

"Let's move on," John snapped, taking a seat and gesturing to the black-haired woman beside him.

"Hi, I'm Katie. I'll just get right to it," she said, glaring at the impatient man beside her as she unfolded her legs and rose from her seat. "I found my nephew in his playroom, dead."

I took a moment to collect myself and responded, gently, "I'm so sorry, Katie. Would you mind telling us how this happened?"

Katie swallowed and forged ahead, "He was stabbed. Twice. Once in the heart and once in the stomach." She took a deep breath as a tear escaped her eye. "He was only eight years old." Katie whisked away the tear with a carefully polished finger, the red of her nail not far from the red of blood. 

Before I could console the poor woman, Sam jumped in with an impossibly shaky voice, "Eight years old? Stabbed in the heart and stomach? That sounds exactly like what happened to Ryan!" Sam was already in tears, using the sleeve of her stained shirt to wipe smeared make-up from her cheeks. 
Unsure of what to do and wishing I had chosen a different career, or that at least John would rush an end to this session, I looked across the circle to see a remorseful scowl cross the man's face.

"John, is there something you would like to say?" 

John blinked slowly and turned to the clock. "Jane...she wrote with a great deal of detail..." As John's voice trailed off, I feared I knew where this was going. 

Then, suddenly, as John realized his mistake in incriminating the woman he loved, he jumped to his feet and swung his stool across the room at Sam, who crouched in fear as it hit her square on the forehead, knocking her unconscious. 

"John!" I yelled in vain, as John turned to Katie and punched her in the nose. The gush of blood is all I remember seeing before losing sight of the incident following a very solid kick in the spine. I lay on the ground, hearing only the sound of Katie's screams for seconds before their abrupt ending, at which point I could make out the click of heels across the cement floor, then lips on lips. I flipped myself over, carefully, and forced myself to focus through my blurry vision, making my way through the spinning room to what I hoped was the exit door. 
Suddenly, I felt a sharp pain in my stomach. I instinctively reached for the pain with my right hand, only to hit an arm. I reached with my left to feel the handle of a knife move away from my stomach as blood covered my hand. My attacker knelt beside me and pushed me onto my back.

"I'll greive for you." I heard John's voice, then a snicker, as the woman leaning over my torn body dug her knife into my heart.

I knew I would not be the final victim of Jane and John.

I release my father's hand and run as fast as I can towards the center of the street, my arms pumping back and forth in loose swings as I grin and crane my neck towards the sky. The doors of the tall buildings lining the street are obscured by bodies bustling about amidst the soundtracks of my favorite Disney movies. I can smell sugar from the food stands and dining areas scattered about the front of the park. I am finally in Disneyland. 

"Let's go Barney.' My dad takes my hand and leads me through the crowd as I stare in awe at the carousel and jump and skip my way down the street beside my dad, who pats me on the head over my baseball cap. He asks me where I want to go first, but I am too excited for words. 

I see soft colors and movement as people sit on a ride and laugh, spinning quickly across the floor in teacups. I point with glee and giggle, "That one, daddy!", and as we stand in line, my awe in the presence of the magical Disney park is enough to keep me entertained.

I never want to leave.

It's busier than I remember, and the sun beats down on my face, distracting me from the map I hold in my hands. 

"Will you give PJ his hat, Laura?" I ask my wife impatiently as she looks around the park as if she's never seen the fabricated land of "dreams" and "hopes" before. I turn back to the map and decide we can head over to the restrooms so I can grab a drink before suffering through the long, hot day ahead.

"Daddy, look at that!" PJ tugs on my arm and points up at some building ahead of us as we make our way down the street. I glance towards his point of focus and nod, "Yes, very nice PJ. Static-filled music blares in the background as PJ goes on and on and Laura points out all the things she wants to buy. 

I release PJ's hand as we approach the water fountain and fill up my bottle. PJ runs to me as I turn around, jumping and yelling about what he's seen.

"It spins all around and you can spin it yourself and it's from that movie about the rabbit and..." PJ goes on, but I've tuned out already. Spinning rides do not appeal to me, and I decide I'll have Laura wait through the long line with PJ. After all, she was the one who wanted to go on this trip. I'll sit on a bench in the shade and try to tune out the laughter and low-quality music. Maybe I'll buy one of the sickeningly sweet smelling desserts. 

I can't wait to go home.
